## Purpose
The FastAPI application entry point: builds the `FastAPI` app, configures logging/CORS/request-ID middleware, registers every API router, and defines the process lifespan (startup restoration + periodic sandbox sweep + graceful shutdown).

## Shape
- Structured JSON logging setup: a per-request `contextvars`-based request ID (`_request_id_var`), a `_RequestIdFilter` that stamps it onto every `LogRecord`, and a `_JsonFormatter` that emits CloudWatch-friendly JSON log lines instead of the previous pipe-delimited text format.
- `lifespan(app)`: an `asynccontextmanager` that on startup logs the DB/LLM-provider config, refuses to boot against an unmigrated schema (except in `ENV=development`), calls `restore_non_terminal_runs()` on the execution engine (wiring several app-layer callback injection points — WS bridge, live-ectx register/unregister, resume cancel event, output-column persisters — onto the engine instance), and starts a periodic `_sandbox_sweep_loop()` background task; on shutdown it cancels the sweep task and delegates to `shutdown_run_infrastructure()`.
- `app = FastAPI(...)` plus `CORSMiddleware` and a `_request_id_middleware` HTTP middleware that adopts or mints `X-Request-ID`.
- ~20 `app.include_router(...)` calls registering every API router (auth, chats, agents, workflows, runs, run_commands, run_stream, handoff, mcp, admin, etc.).
- A `/health` endpoint.

## Why this shape
Inline comments describe deliberate constraints: the engine (kernel) must never import `app.*` (the import-linter-enforced boundary), so `main.py` is the single wiring site that injects app-layer callbacks into the engine instance at startup rather than the engine importing them; the schema-check-before-boot guard exists so production never silently serves traffic against an unmigrated database; and the shutdown teardown is delegated to `app.api.run_shutdown` specifically so `main.py` never reaches into private per-run registries and a teardown failure can't turn a clean exit into a failed uvicorn shutdown.
